name: Kesar India Limited
sector: Real estate, securities trading and overseas goods trading
summary:
Hold — unresolved. Kesar India is a Nagpur-focused real-estate developer that now also has meaningful securities and overseas goods trading, not a pure recurring property-sales compounder. Completed layouts and rising property profit are credible strengths. The decisive risk is the gap between accounting growth, attributable project cash returns and minority capital allocation: FY26 CFO was negative ₹128.13 crore, land advances pending conveyance ₹128.10 crore, and the October promoter swap acquired an existing licensed brand rather than fresh land or cash.
At the dated ₹1089.95 quote and 34,265,970 issued shares, market value is ₹3734.82 crore. A large opportunity is already priced. Ordinary five-year return and entry-price range remain NS, not a buy/sell target, because current financeability and full project obligations cannot be established. The evidence supports further special-situation/property research, not a verified high-quality compounder. Clarified Q1 figures, a complete AS/Ind AS cash bridge and project-level collections, costs, ownership and title/funding schedules could change the assessment.

sections.text:
Kesar India Limited; ISIN INE0L1C01019; BSE 543542; official master symbol KESAR$, series SM. Incorporated 5 November 2003, renamed in 2021; IPO prospectus dated 25 June 2022. The issuer is not similarly named Kesar Enterprises or Kesar Petroproducts. Board migration approval does not prove exchange migration; Q1 notes still describe the process and October master retains SM.
Information cutoff 20 October 2026; market reference 19 October 2026. Price is secondary historical close, not executable live offer. sections.text:
BQS NS, GQS NS, IAS NS. GQS means Growth Quality, and IAS factor P means Price-implied expectations. The 13 canonical factors are scored once: GOV 5, MOAT 4, REV NS, DUR 6, CAP NS, CASH 4, BAL NS, EXEC 5, EARN 5, R NS, D NS, P 3, L 8. No unobserved input is assigned a neutral 5 and no missing weight is redistributed.
BQS known contribution 3.20, coverage 0.68, mathematical bound ['3.52', '6.40']; GQS known 2.35, coverage 0.45, bound ['2.90', '7.85']; IAS known 1.10, coverage 0.20, bound ['1.90', '9.10']. These are not probabilistic ranges or ranked points. Exact Decimal weights and contributions and all factor facts/counterfacts are embedded below.
No GOV≤3 or G1 Fail override applies. CASH 4 does not meet the≤3 value-destruction cap threshold. Moving uncertain GOV or EARN by one point changes known BQS by 0.20 or GQS by 0.15 respectively, without curing missing inputs or gates. sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
Property operations acquire/assemble land, obtain approvals, develop plotted layouts and increasingly propose villas, commercial space and high-rise projects. Cash is committed before sale recognition; bookings, customer advances, progress, conveyance, collections and recognized sales occur at different dates. Every project needs its own ownership, RERA/title, receivable, cost-to-complete and debt/escrow bridge before deriving NAV. Current customer advances ₹3.9347 crore are obligations, not free equity.
FY26 revenue split: property ₹131.0866 crore, securities ₹15.4294 crore, goods ₹29.7667 crore, services ₹0.1442 crore and dividends ₹0.0249 crore. Standalone geographic/property economics differ from the consolidated foreign group. Q1 FY27 foreign revenue ₹148.0886 crore and PBT ₹17.0341 crore dominate consolidated ₹171.0026 crore revenue/₹17.2501 crore PBT; this is not evidence that Nagpur homes sold tenfold faster. Goods turnover, stock finance and counterparty exposure must be separately normalized.
Subsidiaries, LLPs and associates expanded rapidly. A cash subscription can remain within consolidated cash; a purchase from an outside/promoter shareholder can leave the group. Ownership-specific economics and funding cannot be inferred merely from the number of subsidiaries.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
The most plausible advantage is local land access, approvals experience, relationships and recognizable layout branding. Nine completed named layouts are more meaningful than a national real-estate TAM. However, no independent evidence shows persistent selling-price premium, low acquisition cost relative to competitors, superior collection discipline or durable excess project returns. Land scarcity does not automatically give the listed minority a moat when sourcing costs and ownership vary.
Sunteck, Kolte-Patil and Godrej Properties are useful disclosure/competition reference points, not close valuation clones. FY26 presales/collections were ₹3157/1433 crore, ₹2605/2689 crore and ₹34171/19965 crore respectively. These issuers differ materially in scale, city mix, brand, capital access and development-management attribution. Their presentations distinguish bookings and collections, illustrating the missing bridge in Kesar's headline recognized sales. No peer multiple is transplanted mechanically. Kesar's sale to Godrej also illustrates the role of a larger, well-funded counterparty rather than proving equivalent consumer-brand economics.
The brand-company acquisition may consolidate IP rights, but the brand had already been licensed to the listed operating company. Its discounted royalty value cannot be separately added to earnings or property NAV already incorporating brand benefits.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Historical revenue is ₹1.1603 crore FY21, ₹8.4117 crore FY22, ₹15.1862 crore FY23, ₹53.4164 crore FY24, ₹107.7906 crore FY25 and ₹176.4518 crore FY26. These reported endpoints describe exceptional expansion from a tiny base but not six years of identical economic perimeter. FY21 profit itself differs between IPO restatement and later AS comparative; FY24 foreign incorporation, later acquisitions, gross trading and FY26 Ind AS further constrain a comparable organic window. Both five-year and three-year reported CAGRs and annual additions are shown in the calculation appendix, with no trajectory upgrade from one quarter.
Property revenue ₹52.633 crore FY24, ₹76.3643 crore FY25 and ₹131.0866 crore FY26 is a better economic cross-check. Yet the latest amount includes ₹81.0026 crore recognized on a single land transaction. Removing it leaves ₹50.084 crore, below FY24 property revenue, but that is a normalization sensitivity rather than a comparable recurring-sales series because earlier land/bulk mix is not fully bridged. An additional ₹34.7154 crore conditional consideration is unrecognized, not collected or guaranteed value.
REV stays NS: recurring bookings, areas delivered, prices, cancellations, collections and acquired contribution are insufficiently reconciled. It would be equally misleading to score all nominal growth 9 or declare the underlying business shrinking from one adjusted year.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
The management pipeline has tangible named locations but is not an executable backlog. The May table lists 14 completed/ongoing/upcoming projects, including nine completed layouts, three ongoing and two upcoming entries; a further 14 forthcoming names sum to 12.08769 million square feet. Headline 29 projects/15.6 million square feet/₹5100+ crore GDV includes already completed properties and proposals. The 28 named rows do not fully reconcile the 29-project count. Each row is retained with unknown ownership, remaining collections, remaining cost and independently verified title/RERA status explicitly null.
RERA identifiers disclosed for 11 named entries are recorded as company claims, not independently confirmed approvals. Riverdale, Business Park and Mihan show registration in process in the May presentation; subsequent approval status has not been verified from primary project filings. Evaluated ₹4000 crore opportunities are not owned, approved or funded capacity and receive no value.
Land advances ₹128.1015 crore and land/WIP inventory ₹96.4372 crore demonstrate capital commitment, not returns. CAP is NS because neither project cohorts nor a stable organic incremental-return bridge is available. Conditional budgets model cash collections, completion costs and NCI distributions, not an industrial sales-to-working-capital shortcut. GQS cannot be complete without comparable growth and attributable incremental economics.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
The family-controlled company has completed layouts and executed capital raising and acquisitions on dated filings. That is positive delivery evidence. Promoter holding was 67.59% at September 30 with no reported pledge/NDU; after the October swap the calculated holding is 69.23%. Large locked-in holdings constrain practical float. Two executive salaries are approximately ₹0.95 crore each, up 90%; employee median pay also rose 78.70%, so salary growth alone is not evidence of extraction.
The central allocation issue is the ₹155.86 crore purchase of promoter-owned Kesar Lands Private Limited. The target has nil recent turnover and negative book net assets ₹1.008 crore; almost all valuation arises from brand/IP, previously licensed to the listed company from April 2022. The independent valuer uses management projections, 2.5% royalties, terminal value and discount assumptions. A stated 5% maintenance rate appears as about 2% in the royalty table; discount-rate inputs also vary between tables. These weaken precision, not prove fraud. Formal valuation/approval and actual ₹900 issue price above the ₹813.10 valuation are important counterevidence. The higher issue price means fewer shares than a swap solely at the valuer's listed-share estimate.
Promises versus delivery: reported Gateway early completion is a company claim, not an independently obtained completion certificate; preference proceeds had no reported deviation at June; all warrants were converted by September; swap allotted October 14; proposed main-board migration remained unverified as complete. Land/title, approvals, rollout costs and sustained collections remain the key delivery tests. G1 Conditional and GOV 5 reflect mixed stewardship, not an abuse finding.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
FY26 operating EBITDA excluding other income is ₹43.2053 crore and EBIT ₹40.1757 crore, versus consolidated PBT ₹39.5281 crore. Parent PAT ₹30.0037 crore differs from group PAT ₹29.8799 crore by negative NCI ₹0.1238 crore. Current shares imply ₹8.7561 trailing owner EPS, not the historical weighted-average basic ₹11.59/diluted ₹10.04. Shares grew 38.66% from FY25; old holders were diluted 27.88%, distinct percentages.
The cash bridge is pre-WC ₹45.8137 crore less WC ₹160.9362 crore, other non-current financial-asset movement ₹7.2601 crore and cash tax ₹5.7458 crore, giving CFO -₹128.1284 crore. Receivables increased ₹43.5215 crore, inventories ₹87.2588 crore and other current assets ₹141.3375 crore, partly offset by payables ₹107.8686 crore. CFO less all reported capex is -₹133.3248 crore, not a maintenance-FCF estimate. Bank deposits, listed investments and loans have different restrictions and realization risk; they are not all surplus cash. Debt/lease claims and guarantees are kept distinct, with no double deduction of guaranteed group borrowing.
Full current statutory audit/CARO and separate IFC were inspected. Main opinions unmodified and IFC adequate/effective; no default, fraud or wilful-defaulter finding. Fixed-asset location records are being updated. OD quarterly submissions are described as unnecessary, not certified equal to books. Audit-trail operated/no tampering reported, while the retention clause says inapplicable despite citing April 2023 commencement. Land-advance conveyances and interest-free subsidiary-loan valuation are explicit emphases. GST ₹0.5212326 crore is disputed and paid under protest; ₹10 crore Indirapuram performance guarantee is not the entire resolution-plan commitment.
Two material bridges remain unresolved: original FY25 AS CFO -₹7.784 crore versus comparative Ind AS ₹1.4146 crore and cash ₹33.9229 versus ₹30.7364 crore; Q1 parent PAT attribution gap ₹0.561 crore plus March comparator revenue mismatch ₹29.8542 crore. The alternative Q1 file repeats the fields. No corrected statement was located. These are bounded reliability issues, not fraud allegations. Reported balance-based ROCE and incremental EBIT/capital diagnostics are shown as non-scoreable because timing, acquisitions and restatements distort them.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
Current market value ₹3734.82 crore is 124.48×FY26 parent profit, 14.99× March parent book equity and 21.17× revenue. March book ratios are dated before the completed swap and later equity receipts; they are cross-checks, not current NAV. A brand recognized at a transaction valuation would not automatically create equal economic value. No industrial EV/EBITDA target or independent brand addition is used.
The sector-appropriate engine is a conditional five-year cash runoff of future property collections, completion costs, taxes, overhead, legacy receivable/payable settlements, earmarked cash, debt/leases and assumed NCI distributions, plus a separately capitalized trading equity-cash-flow stream. Entry and terminal dates are explicit. Remaining collections ₹500/1000/1800 crore and completion costs 78%/65%/55% are analyst diagnostics, not verified project forecasts. Existing land/inventory is not added again; perpetual land replenishment is deliberately excluded, so results are limited-runoff stress values, not full-company fair prices. All later warrant receipts retain issue-object constraints. The baseline model reserves the remaining ₹6.620515921 crore GCP budget unused; a separate sensitivity permits it only for eligible debt principal, not release into the operating reserve. This conservatism is not a claim that legally permitted GCP use is unavailable. Meanwhile ₹86.683857445 crore project-object funding is available only at actual receipt dates for eligible costs. Pre-entry total cash use is split into explicitly assumed eligible project use and other use, never charged twice. Current resource/claim reconciliation missing means every ordinary return/entry price remains null.
Bear and base breach the cash floor before entry and again during execution; their non-rescue returns stay null even where later notional cash recovers. Separate counterfactual equity rescues include 3% fees, 60% issue-price discount, rounded new shares and holder dilution. Availability/approval is not assumed. Bull has no modeled breach, but its finite-runoff terminal ₹188.09 and annual return -29.63% apply only to that intentionally bounded scenario. No conclusion that all future franchise value is zero follows.
A base-assumption reverse solver finds no funded crossing between ₹500 and ₹20,000 crore future collections; it reports null, not the endpoint as required scale. Simpler earnings algebra shows 15% return at 20× terminal PE requires ₹375.57 crore owner PAT, 65.78% annual growth, no dilution. At 15–30× PE the required profit CAGR ranges 75.60%–52.87%. The swap valuer's DCF is 87.96% terminal-dependent, a useful sensitivity warning rather than an adopted intrinsic value. Two-way collection/cost, linked stress, reserve, receivable, trading multiple and 12/15/18% hurdle tests are fully retained.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest counterargument is that a successful land developer may intentionally absorb cash before monetizing high-value sites; audited debt alone is moderate relative to equity and more than ₹62 crore confirmed post June exercise receipts strengthen resources. A licensed brand may be worth consolidating, and recent foreign trading could diversify profits. A finite runoff deliberately omits future land replenishment, so it is not a complete long-run franchise valuation.
The adverse path combines delayed conveyances/approvals, slower collections on aged receivables, development-cost inflation and lower trading profitability. Obligations remain while customer money is restricted or refundable, suppliers require settlement and guarantees may be called. Recapitalization or forced land sales then transfer future upside away from old shareholders. The model preserves cash deficits rather than pretending they are accessible bank debt. Rescue cases explicitly dilute, but no rescue availability is established.
Qualitative permanent-impairment concern is High because the price requires strong scaling and a complete attributable NAV is unavailable; this is not an empirically estimated probability or a proven insolvency. D remains NS rather than asserting a recovery price from unverified project inputs. A decisive thesis break would be repeated uncorrected financial mismatches plus title/collection failures that exhaust genuinely usable liquidity, not merely a volatile stock price.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
This is not an established 5×/10× thesis. Over the exact five-year calendar horizon, multiplying wealth 5× requires roughly 38% annual appreciation and 10× roughly 58.5%, before personal tax and execution costs. Market value would need to approach ₹18,674 crore or ₹37,348 crore with no new shares. At 20× terminal owner earnings that implies roughly ₹934 crore or ₹1867 crore annual attributable profit, versus ₹30.00 crore FY26.
Gross development value is sales potential before land, construction, taxes, partners, funding and corporate claims, not shareholder wealth. The ₹5100+ crore project headline cannot simply be multiplied by a margin or added to a separately valued brand to justify these outcomes. Foreign trading turnover also cannot be assigned property margins. Extraordinary future execution may create additional projects, but the current sources do not establish the funded, attributable cash economics necessary for a defensible multibagger conclusion. Exact calculations are embedded without subjective scenario probabilities.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
1. Correct/reconcile Q1 owner-profit attribution and March financial-versus-segment comparators; baseline gaps ₹0.561 crore and ₹29.8542 crore. An unreconciled next filing keeps G2 Hold.
2. Publish the full AS-to-Ind AS equity/cash/cash-flow bridge; baseline FY25 CFO difference ₹9.1986 crore. Retain both series until explained.
3. Reconcile each project's opening bookings, cancellations, sales recognition, collections and customer advances, with ownership and completion cost. Baseline 28 named pipeline entries versus 29 headline; no verified consolidated remaining NAV.
4. Close legal title/conveyance of ₹128.1015 crore land advances and verify RERA/escrow status per project. Do not count applications as registrations or completed layouts as unsold pipeline.
5. Track aged receivables ₹47.1933 crore and subsequent collection/allowance. Rising older buckets without cash receipts is an adverse signal.
6. Reconcile current unrestricted cash, earmarked proceeds and all commitments after the confirmed ₹62.0239725 crore post June warrant money. No optional warrant cash remains, and received money does not automatically become unrestricted: the remaining project/GCP object limits must be respected.
7. Separate recurring property profit from bulk land sale, foreign trading margins and nonrecurring loan/valuation gains; publish foreign collections, inventory and counterparty exposures.
8. Explain brand acquisition benefits, old licence terms, valuation sensitivities and incremental royalty savings without double-counting group earnings. Track new RPT land advances and executive pay against cash profit.
9. Verify Indirapuram resolution-plan total obligations, performance guarantees and subsidiary debt/lease maturities; do not equate guarantee amount with purchase price.
10. Before any implementation, refresh exact shares, lot, BSE surveillance/circuits, spread and 100-share depth. Current reference is four lots ₹435,980 below a nominal ₹5 lakh, not a suitability recommendation.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Hold — unresolved, excluded from business-quality, growth-quality and investment point rankings. This is a completed research assessment with material evidence gaps, not an unfinished calculation disguised as an investable score. G1 is Conditional rather than Fail; unmodified audits and formal approvals matter. G2 Hold follows specific quantitative reliability gaps, and G3 Hold follows the missing current resource/obligation bridge, not an actual default finding.
A lower share price may reduce optimistic expectations but cannot fix unverified project ownership, completion liabilities, cash restrictions or inconsistent reporting. Conversely, verified collections, funded project economics, title closure and corrected financial bridges could establish scoreable CAP/BAL/REV and an ordinary return model. Until then no supported entry-price range, order or allocation follows from these conditional stress tests. The analysis is informational, uses a dated quote, and does not constitute individualized financial advice or an execution instruction.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Primary anchors are the FY26/FY25 annual reports including full statutory annexures; FY23/FY24 history and SEBI IPO restatement; issuer Q1 results and duplicate financial file; shareholding/allotment letters; preferential proceeds monitor; acquisition/EGM terms and independent share-swap valuation. Peer issuer/exchange presentations support only specific operational disclosure comparisons. Secondary historical OHLCV is clearly separated from the official security master. Every evidence item maps to source IDs, URLs, locators and retrieved-byte hashes.
Open questions are substantive: current project-level attributable remaining revenue and completion costs; approved RERA/title/escrow status; current unrestricted funds and acquisition/resolution commitments; legacy receivable recovery; foreign trading working-capital and margin sustainability; full Ind AS cash bridge; corrected Q1 owner-profit/segment tables; old brand licence economics and internally inconsistent valuation assumptions; exact current surveillance/live order-book depth. No unseen credit rating, RERA approval or bank statement is represented as verified.
Amounts are ₹crore unless stated. Annual source tables often use ₹lakh and some notes label rupees inconsistently; amounts are checked against audited balance/P&L totals. Model source-safe extracts preserve facts and explicit analyst assumptions, not raw issuer documents. Reproduction validates arithmetic from retained extracts, not fresh authentication of original filings. No raw PDFs, OCR, images, shareholder registers or personal identifiers are included in the analytical backups.

evidence.claim: Audited borrowings 42.0037 crore plus leases 2.3885 crore; cash 31.2436 crore excludes additional bank balances with varying maturity/lien.
evidence.locator: Balance sheet and borrowings/cash notes
evidence.counterevidence_or_limitation: Simple net debt 10.7601 crore is not unrestricted-liquidity proof; management debt-free language is not literal gross-debt fact.

evidence.claim: FY26 main audit unmodified and separate IFC adequate/effective; CARO reports no default, fraud or wilful-defaulter status. Fixed-asset location register updating; bank OD returns described as not required, not independently reconciled.
evidence.locator: FY26 standalone audit pp 106–117, consolidated pp 200–207; FY25 full audit annexures
evidence.counterevidence_or_limitation: No alleged bank-stock mismatch: no quarterly returns were required on management description of OD terms. Audit-trail operated/no tampering reported, but preservation paragraph says not applicable despite referring to April 2023 commencement.

evidence.claim: FY25 original AS CFO -7.784 crore versus Ind AS 1.4146 crore, a 9.1986 crore change; closing cash 33.9229 versus 30.7364 crore.
evidence.locator: FY25 original cash flow and FY26 comparative/transition notes
evidence.counterevidence_or_limitation: Ind AS transition and reclassification are legitimate possible explanations. Full quantitative bridge not located; do not call ordinary consolidation differences errors.

evidence.claim: Q1 total PAT 16.0254 crore differs from reported owner 16.7730 plus NCI -0.1866 by 0.5610 crore. March comparator revenue 84.7993 versus segment 54.9451 crore differs 29.8542 crore.
evidence.locator: Q1 consolidated financial and segment tables; visual check of PDF pages 8–9 in S21
evidence.counterevidence_or_limitation: Total comprehensive 15.8803 crore equals total PAT less OCI. Same fields repeated in alternative issuer file; no correction located. Cannot silently replace owner profit.

evidence.claim: Q1 foreign business contributes 86.60% of revenue and 98.75% of PBT; India segment PBT 0.216 crore. Standalone gain on early repayment of interest-free loan 3.7847 crore is nonrecurring.
evidence.locator: Geographic segment and standalone notes
evidence.counterevidence_or_limitation: Q1 limited review says foreign interim financials not reviewed; annual subsidiary figures separately audited. Consolidated and standalone scope differences are not themselves errors.

evidence.claim: Property revenue 131.0866 crore includes 81.0026 crore recognized Godrej Skyline land consideration;34.7154 crore conditional consideration not recognized.
evidence.locator: Standalone emphasis and revenue notes; total agreement 115.718 crore
evidence.counterevidence_or_limitation: Do not add unrecognized consideration and related land value twice or assume approvals/collection certain.

evidence.claim: Named project tables contain 28 rows against headline 29 projects/15.6 msf/₹5100+ crore GDV; completed projects and proposals included.
evidence.locator: Project tables pp 22–23 and pipeline slides
evidence.counterevidence_or_limitation: Headline GDV is neither attributable remaining revenue nor project NAV. ₹4000 crore evaluated opportunities excluded.

evidence.claim: Related-party Kesar Lands acquisition has nil recent turnover and negative book net assets 1.008 crore; brand valuation 156.866 crore supports 155.858 crore target equity value.
evidence.locator: Acquisition annexure and NAV/relief-from-royalty tables
evidence.counterevidence_or_limitation: Brand existed under April 2022 licence. Independent valuer and shareholder process are counterevidence; no established fraud or illegality.

evidence.claim: Valuer listed-company DCF gets 87.96% of enterprise value from discounted terminal value; FY31 revenue assumption 1833.266 crore. Royalty model text 5% maintenance versus table~2% and discount-rate tables differ.
evidence.locator: DCF cash-flow, WACC and royalty tables
evidence.counterevidence_or_limitation: These are dated management projections, not achieved results. Higher ₹900 issue price versus ₹813.10 valuation means fewer shares issued to promoters than that valuation exchange ratio.

evidence.claim: October 14 noncash swap issues 1,731,752 shares, increasing total to 34,265,970; no cash raised.
evidence.locator: Allotment and original acquisition price
evidence.counterevidence_or_limitation: Shares×₹900=155.85768 crore versus original stated 155.85778 crore; ₹1,000 rounding/document discrepancy, not material conclusion.

evidence.claim: All 7,733,701 warrants converted by September 1; post June exercises 2,362,818 deliver ₹62.0239725 crore balance cash; no remaining optional proceeds.
evidence.locator: Monitoring report and subsequent allotments
evidence.counterevidence_or_limitation: Original loan conversion 10.9999925 crore is noncash. Prior 25% deposits cannot be counted again as fresh conversion cash.

evidence.claim: June issue receipts 211.6955225 crore include noncash converted loans; use 180.4151216 crore and earmarked 31.280400866 crore reconcile.
evidence.locator: Use-of-proceeds and unutilized balance tables
evidence.counterevidence_or_limitation: Remaining issue objects total ₹93.304373366 crore:₹86.683857445 crore land/development and ₹6.620515921 crore GCP. These equal June unspent plus later exercise money; conversion does not release object restrictions. Monitor reports no deviation but is not a credit rating or free-cash certification.

evidence.claim: June monitor includes related-party land advances 7.421953 crore and GCP loan repayments 11.6787319 crore; funds include FD/sweep balances and subsidiary cash.
evidence.locator: Notes 5–6 and object deployment
evidence.counterevidence_or_limitation: Shareholder authorization is reported; advances still require title, end-use and ownership verification. Do not count subsidiary subscription twice within consolidated cash.

evidence.claim: September promoter 67.59%, no disclosed pledge/NDU; after swap computed 69.23%. Issued shares grow 38.66% vs FY25; old-holder dilution 27.88%.
evidence.locator: Shareholding totals and capital roll-forward
evidence.counterevidence_or_limitation: Postswap percentage is calculated, not a new audited shareholding filing. Lock-in further constrains immediately tradable float.

evidence.claim: June valuer provisional cash 56.169 crore and debt 32.415 crore are not a full audited October cash/obligation bridge.
evidence.locator: Provisional balance and post-June office acquisition
evidence.counterevidence_or_limitation: Published later warrant receipts are real; remaining uncertainty is current encumbrances, acquisitions, completion commitments and spending, not a demand for private daily bank statements.

evidence.claim: Bank guarantees 11 crore include 10 crore Indirapuram resolution-performance guarantee; corporate guarantee drawn 10.5506 crore with 45 crore sanction. GST 0.5212326 crore paid under protest.
evidence.locator: Contingencies and bank guarantee notes
evidence.counterevidence_or_limitation: Group guaranteed borrowing cannot be deducted a second time if already in group debt. Performance guarantee is not the complete resolution-plan purchase commitment. GST disputed, not proven liability.

evidence.claim: 60/60 common-calendar sessions have secondary BSE observations, mean turnover proxy 8.5009 crore but median 1.87979 crore;100-share lot costs ₹108,995.
evidence.locator: Extracted dated OHLCV and exact issuer master row
evidence.counterevidence_or_limitation: Close× volume is not actual traded value; spreads/live depth/direct BSE surveillance not verified. Missing NSE issuer rows are never zero trades.

evidence.claim: Sunteck FY26 presales 3157 crore/collections 1433 crore; Kolte-Patil 2605/2689; Godrej 34171/19965.
evidence.locator: FY26 operational highlights
evidence.counterevidence_or_limitation: Much larger/different geographies; gross/attributable/DMA collection definitions differ. Used for disclosure and competition comparison, not blind P/E or EV/GDV transplant.

evidence.claim: FY21–FY23 standalone base is tiny and restated; FY24 foreign subsidiary, FY25/26 acquisitions and FY26 Ind AS change comparability.
evidence.locator: Historical annual statements and IPO restatement
evidence.counterevidence_or_limitation: FY21 IPO PAT 0.0119 crore versus later AS comparative 0.2165 crore. Reported nominal CAGRs remain descriptive, not a verified organic demand score.

evidence.claim: FY26 two executive salaries each approximately 0.95 crore, up 90%; CFO remuneration up 100%; median employee remuneration rose 78.70%; permanent employees 71.
evidence.locator: Director appointment profile and remuneration annexure p 78
evidence.counterevidence_or_limitation: Employee pay also rose strongly; remuneration increase alone is not evidence of extraction. Formal policy approval reported.

evidence.claim: Conditional finite-project runoff scenarios require unverified remaining collections, costs and NCI ownership. Bear and base breach before entry and during execution; both non-rescue returns null.
evidence.locator: Analyst model assumptions tied to dated opening claims, not a source forecast
evidence.counterevidence_or_limitation: Bull remains a limited-runoff diagnostic, not valuation of perpetual future land replenishment. No ordinary investment return or entry price justified.
